summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Apomixis (Agamospermy): Asexual seed formation without meiosis or syngamy (Adventive embryony from nucellar cells in Citrus/Mango, Apospory, Diplospory). Parthenocarpy: Seedless fruit development without ovular fertilization (Banana, Grapes; induced by auxins/GAs). Polyembryony: Presence of >1 embryo per seed (Citrus, Leeuwenhoek 1719).

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 9.1 Mechanisms of Apomixis (Agamospermy)

Apomixis is a genetically determined mode of reproduction where seeds are formed without the processes of meiosis and syngamy, producing clonal maternal offspring.
1. **Adventive Embryony (Sporophytic Agamospermy)**:
   - Diploid maternal cells of the **Nucellus or Integuments** actively divide, protrude into the embryo sac cavity, and develop directly into embryos.
   - *Examples*: *Citrus, Mangifera (Mango), Opuntia*.
2. **Apospory (Gametophytic Agamospermy)**:
   - A vegetative diploid somatic cell of the nucellus develops directly into an unreduced ($2n$) embryo sac without meiosis.
   - *Examples*: *Hieracium, Parthenium*.
3. **Diplospory**:
   - The Megaspore Mother Cell (MMC) fails to undergo meiosis (or undergoes an unreduced division) and directly produces an unreduced ($2n$) embryo sac.
   - *Examples*: *Taraxacum (Dandelion), Asteraceae*.

### 9.2 Parthenocarpy & Polyembryony
- **Parthenocarpy**: Formation and development of a fleshy fruit without fertilization of ovules, producing **seedless fruits** (e.g., *Banana, Grapes, Pineapple*). Can be induced commercially by spraying with **Auxins and Gibberellins**.
- **Polyembryony**: The occurrence of more than one embryo inside a single seed (first discovered by **Antonie van Leeuwenhoek in 1719** in orange seeds). Can arise via **Cleavage polyembryony** (proembryo splits, e.g., *Pinus*) or **Adventive polyembryony** (nucellar budding in *Citrus*).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Hybrid Seed Technology Advantage
conceptBreakdown.title: Hybrid Seed Technology Advantage
conceptBreakdown.content: If hybrid crop varieties can be engineered with apomictic genes, farmers can save and sow seeds year after year without segregation and loss of hybrid vigor (heterosis), eliminating the expensive need to repurchase hybrid seeds annually.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Pseudogamy in Apomicts
conceptBreakdown.title: Pseudogamy in Apomicts
conceptBreakdown.content: In some apomictic plants (Pseudogamy), pollination is still required to stimulate the primary endosperm nucleus or trigger ovary growth, even though the male gamete does not fertilize the egg cell.
